description: Differential corpus for the incumbent twitterapi-proxy on ardenone-cluster, captured live over the tailnet ingress (Traefik entryPoint `vpn`, 100.71.31.73:8444) on 2026-07-31. Supersedes the bf-kki8 corpus, which was written against an assumed Twitter API v2 shape and matched nothing this service does (see docs/research/twitterapi-proxy-deployment.md §7). The incumbent is a wholly generic pass-through caching reverse proxy for api.twitterapi.io with no Twitter semantics: it defines exactly one endpoint of its own (GET /health, local, empty body, no upstream call) and forwards every other path verbatim. Callers send no credential — the proxy strips inbound `x-api-key` and `authorization` and injects the key server-side — so entries carry a secret *ref* describing how SEAM must inject (kind=header, name=x-api-key), never a value. Entries deliberately omit `expect.status`, so the plain differential rule (incumbent.status == seam.status) applies; the status verified live is recorded in each entry's description instead, which is a stricter check than pinning. Reproduce with scripts/capture-twitterapi-proxy.sh.

entries.description: Control header `X-Cache-Bypass: 1` forces a cache miss and a fresh, BILLED upstream call. Verified live 2026-07-31: an already-cached request that returns `x-cache-status: hit` returns `x-cache-status: miss` with this header set. Skipped by default because it is the one entry that cannot be replayed for free — each replay bills twitterapi.io credits on both the incumbent and the SEAM side. Unskip only for a deliberate, budgeted bypass-semantics run.

expect.skip: Bypasses the cache by design, so every replay bills upstream credits on both targets. Enable deliberately, not in CI.

entries.description: Security invariant: the proxy strips inbound `x-api-key` and `authorization` (FORBIDDEN_FORWARD_HEADERS) and substitutes its own key, so a caller can neither leak nor override it. The two credential headers below are deliberate decoys, not real secrets. Verified live 2026-07-31: both requests returned 200 with `x-cache-status: hit`, i.e. the bogus values changed nothing. SEAM must strip identically; the harness leak check additionally proves the real injected key never appears in the response.

Upstream 400 for a missing required query param. Verified live 2026-07-31: `GET /twitter/user/info` with no userName → 400, content-length 33, body {"detail":"userName is required"}. Note the error shape is a bare {detail} object — NOT the {status,msg,data} success envelope. Deterministic, so the body is compared: non-2xx responses are never cached, and this payload is a fixed string.

Upstream 404 for a path twitterapi.io does not serve, proving the proxy's catch-all fallback forwards unknown paths rather than answering them itself. Verified live 2026-07-31: 404, content-length 22, body {"detail":"Not Found"}. Deterministic, so the body is compared. Errors are never cached, so this entry always exercises a real upstream round-trip (twitterapi.io does not bill non-2xx).

The only endpoint the proxy defines itself. Routed before the catch-all fallback so liveness/readiness probes never burn an API credit. Verified live 2026-07-31: 200, `content-length: 0`, EMPTY body, and notably NO `x-cache-status` header (no cache path is taken) and none of the upstream Cloudflare headers. Takes no secret: there is no upstream call. Body is compared — empty is the assertion.

Proves the method is forwarded verbatim, not just GET. Uses an unknown path so there is no write side effect and nothing is billed: twitterapi.io's real write ops (the *_v2 endpoints) cost $0.002-0.003 each AND actually post to X, so they must never appear in a replayed corpus. Verified live 2026-07-31: POST /twitter/nonexistent/endpoint → 404, content-length 22, {"detail":"Not Found"} — identical to the GET, confirming the fallback is method-agnostic. Deterministic, so the body is compared.

Advanced tweet search, the heaviest read path. Verified live 2026-07-31: 200, bare {"tweets":[...]} payload with NO {status,msg,data} wrapper. Body ignored: a Latest-sorted search re-runs against a moving index, and with no cursor it is a front-page request (FRONT_PAGE_TTL_SECS=300), so the incumbent's and SEAM's independent caches cannot be expected to hold the same result set.

Fetch tweets by id — the replacement for the bf-kki8 entry that used the nonexistent /2/tweets/{id} path. Verified live 2026-07-31: 200, bare {"tweets":[...]} payload with NO {status,msg,data} wrapper. Body ignored: the tweet text is immutable but its engagement counters (likeCount, retweetCount, viewCount) tick continuously, and with no cursor this is a front-page request (300s TTL), so two independently-cached proxies will disagree.

THE deterministic anchor of this corpus, and the only entry whose live-data body is compared byte-for-byte. A request carrying a non-empty `cursor` is NOT a front-page request, so it escapes FRONT_PAGE_TTL_SECS=300 and is cached forever — the page is therefore frozen and identical on every replay. Verified live 2026-07-31: first call `x-cache-status: miss`, repeat `hit`, and a repeat with the two query params REORDERED also `hit`, confirming the cache key normalizes query order. Cursor value came from the `next_cursor` of the front-page call.

Cursorless follower page — the front-page counterpart to user-followers-cursor-paged, kept so the 300s-TTL path is exercised alongside the cache-forever one. Verified live 2026-07-31: 200, flat payload {"followers":[...],"has_next_page":true,"next_cursor":"...","status":"success","msg":"success","code":0} — status/msg sit at the top level here, NOT wrapping a `data` object. Body ignored: the follower list and next_cursor both move.

User lookup by handle — the replacement for the bf-kki8 entry that used the nonexistent /2/users/by/username/{handle} path. Verified live 2026-07-31: 200 with the {"status":"success","msg":"success","data":{...}} envelope; data carries id, userName, followers, createdAt, pinnedTweetIds, isBlueVerified, etc. Body ignored: `followers`/`statusesCount`/`favouritesCount` change minute to minute and, being cursorless, the entry re-fetches every 300s.

A user's recent tweets — the replacement for the bf-kki8 /2/users/{id}/tweets entry. Verified live 2026-07-31: 200 with a THIRD envelope variant, {"status":"success","code":0,"msg":"success","data":{"pin_tweet":...,"tweets":[...]}} plus top-level has_next_page/next_cursor — note the extra `code` field that /twitter/user/info does not return. Body ignored: new tweets arrive constantly and this is a cursorless 300s-TTL entry.
